subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should OpenClaw add one default-on channel/gateway runtime policy for silence beacons plus response-delivery confirmation/retry/no-response alerts, or keep the work split across narrower heartbeat and durable-delivery contracts?
rationale: The request adds new default channel-visible behavior, config, retries, alerts, and cross-channel ACK semantics; source inspection can show the gap but cannot choose those product and compatibility defaults safely.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split implementation
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate policy while landing narrower pieces through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830.

options.title: Close after naming canonical trackers
options.body: Close this only after maintainers explicitly designate which open issues own the silence-watchdog and delivery-confirmation halves.

options.title: Sponsor one combined core feature
options.body: Define the config, default-on behavior, retry/alert semantics, and cross-channel ACK contract here before implementation starts.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split implementation
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate policy while landing narrower pieces through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830.

likelyOwner.reason: The maintainer-labeled durable final fallback issue is the most explicit open contract owner for the delivery-confirmation half of this umbrella.
